item.title: Former Prince Andrew released after arrest in Epstein-related probe
item.description:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former Prince Andrew, was released by British police late Thursday after being held for approximately 11 hours following his arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office, Thames Valley Police confirmed.

The arrest, which occurred on Mountbatten-Windsor's 66th birthday at Wood Farm on King Charles III's Sandringham estate in Norfolk, marks the first time the former royal has been detained by police. He departed a police station in a black Range Rover Thursday evening after being released "under investigation," meaning he has neither been charged nor exonerated.

item.title: North Korea opens 9th Party Congress with Kim claiming economic success
item.description:
North Korea convened its Ninth Party Congress on Thursday, the country's largest political gathering held every five years, according to the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

In his opening speech, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un declared that the economy had overcome recession and the country accomplished major economic goals over the past five years, KCNA reported. The claim marks a striking contrast to the 8th Party Congress in January 2021, when Kim acknowledged that his previous five-year economic plan had failed "in almost all sectors."

item.title: Italy considers adding 100,000 military personnel by 2044
item.description:
Italy's defense ministry is weighing a sweeping proposal to increase military personnel by more than 60 percent over the next 18 years, according to a document seen by Reuters. The plan, presented this week to Defence Minister Guido Crosetto, would grow the combined strength of the army, navy, and air force from approximately 170,000 to 275,000 personnel, including a 15,000-strong reserve, at an estimated cost of around six billion euros.

The proposal, drafted by military experts, lays the groundwork for an ambitious overhaul of the Italian armed forces that officials expect to unveil by the end of March. If implemented, personnel costs would rise to nearly 15 billion euros from the current 8.8 billion euros, with the expansion phased in gradually through 2044.

item.title: Iran warns UN that Trump remarks raise risk of conflict
item.description:
Iran has declared in a letter to UN Secretary-General António Guterres that President Donald Trump's recent rhetoric signals "a real risk of military aggression" and warned that Tehran will target the bases, facilities, and assets of any hostile force if it faces an attack, according to Iran's permanent mission to the United Nations.

The letter, sent Thursday, emphasized that while Iran does not seek war, any military aggression would be met with a decisive response. Iran's warning follows Trump's announcement at the inaugural meeting of his Board of Peace that Tehran has approximately 10 days to reach a deal with Washington or face potential military strikes.

item.title: Venezuela passes amnesty bill for political prisoners
item.description:
Venezuela's National Assembly on Thursday approved an amnesty bill that could lead to the release of politicians, activists, lawyers, and many others detained for political reasons, according to the Associated Press. The measure, which passed unanimously after two weeks of negotiations, effectively acknowledges that the government has held hundreds of people in prison for political motivations — a stark reversal for a country whose authorities denied the existence of political prisoners for decades.

Acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who proposed the legislation in late January under pressure from the Trump administration following the U.S. military capture of Nicolás Maduro on January 3, is expected to sign the bill into law.

item.title: NASA says 15,000 'city-killer' asteroids remain untracked with no defense ready
item.description:
Roughly 15,000 asteroids large enough to obliterate a city are orbiting near Earth undetected, and humanity has no spacecraft ready to deflect any of them. That was the blunt assessment delivered this week by NASA officials at the American Association for the Advancement of Science annual meeting in Phoenix, Arizona.

Dr. Kelly Fast, NASA's acting planetary defense officer, told conference attendees that scientists have identified an estimated 25,000 asteroids measuring at least 140 meters in diameter — large enough to cause catastrophic regional destruction — but current detection systems have catalogued only about 40 percent of them. "What keeps me up at night are the asteroids we don't know about," Fast said, according to the Washington Times. "It's the ones in between that could do regional damage".

item.title: World leaders set to issue joint AI stance at India summit
item.description:
Dozens of world leaders, tech executives, and policymakers gathered in New Delhi this week for the India AI Impact Summit 2026, the largest global AI summit to date and the first held in a developing nation. As the five-day event at Bharat Mandapam nears its close, participants are expected to deliver a joint declaration on Friday outlining a shared approach to managing artificial intelligence.

The summit — the fourth in an annual series following gatherings in the United Kingdom, South Korea, and France — drew more than 20 heads of state, over 100 country delegations, and tens of thousands of attendees from across the AI industry.

item.title: NASA completes Artemis II rehearsal, clearing path for moon launch
item.description:
NASA wrapped up a successful wet dress rehearsal for the Artemis II mission on Wednesday night, clearing a major hurdle in the agency's push to send astronauts around the moon for the first time in more than 50 years. The rehearsal concluded at 10:16 p.m. EST on February 19, ending as planned at T-29 seconds in the simulated countdown.

The test marked a turnaround from a troubled first attempt earlier this month. During the initial wet dress rehearsal on February 2, a liquid hydrogen leak at the base of the Space Launch System rocket forced NASA to cut the countdown short at the T-5 minute, 15-second mark, prompting the agency to wave off its February launch window entirely.

item.title: World leaders adopt AI governance declaration at India summit
item.description: Dozens of world leaders, ministers, and tech executives gathered in New Delhi this week for the India AI Impact Summit, the largest global AI gathering to date and the first in a developing nation. The five-day event at Bharat Mandapam culminated on Friday, February 20, with the expected adoption of a Leaders' Declaration outlining shared commitments to responsible, inclusive, and collaborative AI governance.

item.title: New studies warn Antarctica faces irreversible ice and ecosystem loss
item.description: A pair of major studies published this week paint a stark picture of Antarctica's future, warning that without rapid cuts to greenhouse gas emissions, the continent faces cascading ice loss and ecological destruction that would be irreversible on any human timescale.

item.title: Gold hovers near $5,000 as Iran tensions and Fed outlook collide
item.description:
Gold clung to the $5,000-an-ounce level on Friday, caught between safe-haven demand fueled by escalating U.S.-Iran brinkmanship and a strengthening dollar that has put the metal on course for a weekly loss. Spot gold dipped slightly to around $4,983 per ounce in early Asian trading, down roughly 1% for the week, while U.S. gold futures for April held just above $5,000.

The tug-of-war encapsulates a market hypersensitive to two fast-moving storylines: a potential military confrontation in the Middle East and a Federal Reserve that appears in no hurry to cut interest rates.

item.title: New nanodevices turn evaporation and pressure into electricity
item.description: Two teams of researchers — one in Switzerland, the other in Australia — have independently developed nanodevices capable of generating electricity from everyday physical processes, offering fresh avenues for sustainable, battery-free power. Both studies, published this week in Nature Communications, demonstrate how nanoscale engineering can turn evaporating saltwater and mechanical pressure into usable energy.

item.title: Ukraine eyes billions in defense exports after first wartime sales approved
item.description:
Ukraine expects to export "several billion dollars" in military goods and services in 2026, a senior defense official told Reuters, marking a dramatic reversal from the arms export ban Kyiv imposed after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Davyd Aloian, deputy secretary of Kyiv's National Security and Defence Council, said a state commission approved the majority of 40 export applications from defense producers earlier this month — the first wartime export licenses granted since the war began. "Taking into account ready-made products, spare parts, components, and services that can be provided, it amounts to several billion dollars," Aloian told Reuters in an interview published Thursday.

The export potential is "significantly higher" than pre-war levels, Aloian said. Before 2022, Ukraine typically ranked among the world's top 15 arms exporters, with average annual sales of roughly $400 million over three decades, according to data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.

item.title: India, Germany post manufacturing-led PMI gains in February
item.description: Flash purchasing managers' surveys released Friday showed private sector activity in both India and Germany accelerating in February, driven in each case by a pickup in manufacturing output that lifted composite PMI readings to multi-month highs.

item.title: India signs U.S.-led Pax Silica pact on AI and chips
item.description:
Dozens of world leaders and ministers gathered at the India AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi this week, with a Leaders' Declaration expected to be adopted Friday outlining a shared roadmap for global AI governance and collaboration. The five-day summit — the fourth in a series of global AI convenings and the first hosted by a developing nation — drew heads of state from 20 countries, hundreds of tech executives, and an estimated 250,000 visitors to the Bharat Mandapam convention center.

The event produced a flurry of diplomatic and commercial activity, headlined by the signing of the Pax Silica Declaration between India and the United States, massive investment pledges from major technology firms, and the unveiling of a new U.S. initiative to deploy AI expertise abroad.

item.title: New study warns Antarctic Peninsula faces irreversible damage without rapid emissions cuts
item.description: A new study modeling the best- and worst-case futures for the Antarctic Peninsula warns that the choices made this decade will determine Antarctica's fate for centuries — and that only aggressive emissions reductions can prevent catastrophic and irreversible transformations in one of the planet's most vulnerable regions.

item.title: US 'totally' rejects global AI governance at New Delhi summit
item.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres used the closing day of the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on Friday to formally announce that 40 members have been confirmed for the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, a body he said would work to "make human control a technical reality — not a slogan."

The declaration came on the final day of the five-day summit — the fourth annual global AI gathering, and the first to be hosted in a developing country — where dozens of heads of state, tech executives, and ministers gathered to debate how to govern a technology advancing faster than the institutions trying to regulate it.

item.title: Gold tops $5,000 as Trump's Iran ultimatum fuels safe-haven rush
item.description: Gold prices pushed above $5,000 an ounce on Friday, propelled by escalating tensions between the United States and Iran and persistent uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's interest rate path. The advance came after President Donald Trump gave Tehran a 10-to-15-day deadline to reach a nuclear deal, warning of "bad things" if diplomacy fails.

item.title: Guterres unveils UN panel to ensure 'human control' of AI
item.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Friday called for "less hype, less fear" over artificial intelligence as he unveiled the mission of a new international panel of experts, telling leaders gathered in New Delhi that its goal is to "make human control a technical reality — not a slogan."

Speaking at the AI Impact Summit, the first global AI gathering of its scale hosted in a Global South nation, Guterres said the United Nations General Assembly had confirmed the 40 members of the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, a body designed to serve as the AI equivalent of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.

"We are barrelling into the unknown," Guterres said. "That requires meaningful human oversight in every high-stakes decision" and "clear accountability — so responsibility is never outsourced to an algorithm."

item.title: Global stocks trade mixed as AI fears and Iran tensions collide
item.description:
Global markets traded in mixed fashion on Friday as two forces — deepening anxiety over artificial intelligence's disruptive potential and escalating tensions between the United States and Iran — pulled investors in opposite directions.

In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.1% to close at 56,825.70 as banking and financial stocks slumped, dragged lower by concerns over private lending firms exposed to businesses vulnerable to AI displacement. Hong Kong's Hang Seng slid as trading resumed following the Lunar New Year break, while mainland Chinese markets remained shuttered through next week. South Korea's Kospi bucked the trend, surging 2.2% as defense stocks, led by Hanwha Aerospace, jumped 8.6% on expectations of rising global military spending. In Europe, the pan-European Stoxx 600 edged up 0.2%, approaching an all-time high, while the FTSE 100 gained 0.3% and France's CAC 40 rose 0.5%. U.S. futures pointed to a modestly higher open.
